HasExtraCardText.rationale: presentation only: read solely by EnchantmentModel.DynamicExtraCardText (EnchantmentModel.cs:60-81) and the card-UI nodes; no game-state reader. Out of scope per the shared contract's 'presentation/animation' waiver.

CanEnchant.maps_to: GoopyEnchantment.can_enchant (enchantments.py:285-287) -- base plus `"defend" in card.tags`, matching Goopy.cs:16-23. Enchantment.can_enchant (enchantments.py:51-61) + the subclass override. Base CanEnchant (EnchantmentModel.cs:273-294) rejects CardType 4/5/6 (Status/Curse/Quest), then CanEnchantCardType, then an Unplayable card whose pile is PileType.Deck, then a card that already has a (non-stackable) enchantment. The sim folds CanEnchantCardType into each subclass's own can_enchant and replaces the pile-qualified Unplayable test with an unconditional `not card.is_playable` -- equal in practice because every ported grant enchants a DECK card (probe `grants`).

EnchantBlockAdditive.maps_to: GoopyEnchantment.modify_block_additive (enchantments.py:298-301) -- returns `amount - 1` for its own card, matching Goopy.cs:44-47's `base.Amount - 1`. Additive-only, so BR-1's phase difference cannot bite here: base + sum(adds) is the same fold either way (executed control in `py audit/tools/enchantment_probes.py order`). First-play block with Amount 1 is 5 in both (`py audit/tools/enchantment_probes.py goopy`).

AfterCardPlayed.maps_to: GoopyEnchantment.on_card_played (enchantments.py:303-305) -- `amount += 1` for its own card, matching Goopy.cs:30-42's `base.Amount++`. The C# line the sim has no counterpart for, `base.Card.DeckVersion.Enchantment.Amount++` (Goopy.cs:37-40), is a no-op for the sim: the sim has ONE Enchantment object shared by the run and the combat, so the growth already persists (executed: `py audit/tools/enchantment_probes.py goopy` -- Amount is 2 after one play and survives reset())
AfterCardPlayed.issue: Per-replay firing. See guard EG1: C# runs AfterCardPlayed once per Replay iteration, the sim's on_card_played once per card play. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/enchantment_probes.py replay`): Goopy(1) on a Defend played twice by the ported Throwing Axe relic leaves Amount at 2 in the sim and 3 in the game, and the player gains 10 block instead of 11 (game: 5 on the first play, then Amount becomes 2 so 5 + 1 = 6 on the second).

guards.what: FOUR-VERB COVERAGE (enchant / upgrade+downgrade / transform / copy) -- stated explicitly so the hole cannot reopen silently. Verb 3, TRANSFORM: CardCmd.Transform (CardCmd.cs:369-451) removes the original from its pile and adds a freshly-built replacement; it never touches Enchantment, and the destroyed original takes its enchantment with it
guards.maps_to: TRANSFORM verdict: FAITHFUL, both engines drop the enchantment. C#: CardCmd.Transform's loop takes `item.GetReplacement(rng)`, calls `item.Original.RemoveFromCurrentPile()` (CardCmd.cs:400) and adds the replacement (CardCmd.cs:437/440); the word Enchantment does not appear anywhere in the method, and neither AfterTransformedFrom nor AfterTransformedTo (CardModel.cs:1625-1631, both empty virtuals -- SovereignBlade is the only override in the source) moves it. So the enchantment dies with the original. SIM: run.transform_card (run.py:406-470) and CardCmd.transform_to_random (cmds.py:415-449) both build the replacement with `make_card(...)`, which carries no enchantment. EXECUTED, this unit: `py -c "import sys,random;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.run import RunState;from sts2_rl.cards import make_card;from sts2_rl.enchantments import make_enchantment;r=RunState(rng=random.Random(0));c=make_card('defend');r.deck=[c];e=make_enchantment('goopy');e.amount=2;e.attach(c);n=r.transform_card(c,into=make_card('bash'));print(n.id, n.enchantment)"` -> `bash None`, matching C#. The in-combat twin (CardCmd.transform_to_random on a Sharp'd Strike) also prints a replacement with `enchantment=None`. Same result for all 17 ids. COVERAGE TABLE for this unit -- (1) ENCHANT: the CanEnchantCardType hook entry plus the reachability guard above. (2) UPGRADE / DOWNGRADE: settled in this record's own creature_card_cmds step-52 entry (this enchantment's attach() mutates a STATIC card property, so a card rebuild can drop it). (3) TRANSFORM: this entry, faithful. (4) COPY: guard EG2, gap. All four verbs are now on the record; before this pass transform and copy were 0/17.

guards.what: EG2: card COPY drops the enchantment. C# CardModel.CreateClone (CardModel.cs:2168) -> MutableClone -> DeepCloneFields re-attaches the source card's enchantment onto the copy -- CardModel.cs:1204-1209 `(EnchantmentModel)Enchantment.ClonePreservingMutability()`, `Enchantment = null`, `EnchantInternal(clone, clone.Amount)` -- and does the same for the Affliction two lines down (1210-1215). CreateClone itself throws unless the card sits in a COMBAT pile (CardModel.cs:2170-2173), so every copy site is a combat-pile copy. The sim's copy sites rebuild the card from its class and carry only the upgrade level.
guards.issue: MECHANISM EG2, one verdict at every site (rule 3). FIVE ported sim copy sites drop the enchantment, each a `type(card)()` / `make_card(card.id)` rebuild plus a re-upgrade loop with no `card.enchantment` carry: cards/trash_heap_cards.py:18-24 `_clone` (Dual Wield, DualWield.cs:35), powers.py:827-830 (JugglingPower.cs:48), relics/music_box.py:46-48 (MusicBox.cs:78), cards/anger.py:36-38 (Anger.cs:27) and relics/burning_sticks.py:30-32 (BurningSticks.cs:49). All five map to a C# `CreateClone()` call, so all five are the same defect. The sim's OTHER copy paths are correct and are what makes this a bug rather than a design choice: relics/bing_bong.py:37 and events/reflections.py:52 use `copy.deepcopy` (the enchantment rides along), relics/paels_growth.py:39-46 re-attaches Clone by hand, and the per-combat deck copy (run.py:1136 `copy.deepcopy`) carries it too. EXECUTED, this unit: `py -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from sts2_rl.cards import make_card;from sts2_rl.cards.trash_heap_cards import _clone;from sts2_rl.enchantments import make_enchantment;c=make_card('defend');e=make_enchantment('goopy');e.amount=2;e.attach(c);print(type(c.enchantment).__name__, _clone(c).enchantment)"` -> `GoopyEnchantment None`. The same one-liner run over all 17 ids prints `None` for every one of the 16 that any probe card accepts (souls needs an Exhaust card, so it was run against fiend_fire). RULE 6, both legs -- reachability of the copy site for THIS unit: SKILL-only and further Defend-TAGGED (Goopy.cs:16-21 `card.Tags.Contains(CardTag.Defend)`; executed matrix A/P/S = False/False/True), so Dual Wield CANNOT reach it -- the reachable site is relics/burning_sticks.py:30-32 (the first SKILL exhausted each combat), and it is a tight fit rather than a coincidence: Goopy is the enchantment that ADDS Exhaust to the Defend (enchantments.py:289-291), so the enchanted card is exactly the card Burning Sticks fires on. Every one of the five sites is ported and reachable (Dual Wield from the ported Trash Heap event pool, events/trash_heap.py:17; Anger from the Ironclad common pool; Juggling from cards/juggling.py; Music Box and Burning Sticks are ported relics). LIVENESS: LIVE. The game's Burning Sticks copy of a Goopy'd Defend keeps Goopy -- it exhausts and carries the grown block bonus; the sim's copy is a plain Defend that neither exhausts nor blocks extra. Grant path is the ported Pael's Claw relic (relics/paels_claw.py). SECONDARY (false docstring): `_clone`'s docstring claims it "mirrors CreateClone for the sim's needs". It does not -- CreateClone carries the enchantment AND the affliction; `_clone` carries neither. Fifth entry in this stream's false-docstring list.
